Follow-up to strategy5_roc_ema_macd_stoch_sweep.md. All 50 Nifty 50 stocks, 5 timeframes, delivery buys at the candle close, FYERS charges only, ₹1,00,000 per trade, 1 Jan 2023 – 26 Oct 2026 (15/30-min from 1 Dec 2025). Education, not investment advice. Full report (ROC tables per timeframe, EMA tables, every setting positive in both periods, finalists with charges by type): ../../../projects/trading-equation-backtests/reports/STRATEGY5_ROC_EMA_REPORT.md. Every finalist trade: reports/strategy5/roc_ema_final_trades.csv.

1. Rules

Buy at the candle close when: ROC(length) > level % · close above the EMA (buy candle only, or all of the last 5 candles) · MACD 12/26/9 histogram bigger than the previous bar · Stoch RSI 3/3/14/14 blue crosses above orange, blue below 50. Sell as soon as blue touches orange during a later candle.

Tried: ROC length 10, 20, 30, 50, 100, 150, 200 × level 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 15% × EMA 20, 50, 100, 150, 200 × EMA rule (1 or 5 candles) = 560 settings × 5 timeframes. Train 2023–24, test 2025–26 (15/30-min: Dec 2025–May 2026 / Jun–Oct 2026).

3. Daily: ROC length is what matters

Test-period (2025–26) net ₹, EMA 100, buy candle only:

ROC length> 2%> 3%> 5%> 7%> 10%
10+45k+74k+42k+20k+9k
20+5k+16k+34k+49k+27k
50−36k−6k−8k+18k+42k
100 (yours)−82k−67k−82k−63k−25k
200−74k−70k−80k−129k−148k
  • Short look-backs (10–20 days) keep working in 2025–26; long ones (100–200 days, including your 100) lose. In 2023–24 almost everything made money (a strong rally), so the test years are what separate good from bad settings.
  • ROC 20 at 3–7% works with every EMA length: total +₹1.01L to +₹1.78L, and +₹12k to +₹53k in 2025–26 alone. That's a whole block of neighbouring settings, not one lucky number.
  • EMA length and the 5-candle rule matter much less than the ROC look-back (shorter EMAs 20/50 slightly better).

  • ROC 20 > 7 + EMA 50 made money in 2023, 2024 and 2025, was nearly flat in 2026 (−₹4k), and still made +₹1.08L without its best 3 trades. Random buys with the same ROC/EMA filter made +₹33k, so the timing adds real value (beats 97% of runs).

How much money it really needs (ROC 20 > 7, EMA 50, daily)

₹1,00,000 is per trade, per company. Several companies can be open at once: up to 13 at the same time (28 Dec 2023), so taking every signal needed ₹12.9 lakh. Most of the time far fewer were open (none on 39% of days, 1–2 on most others; trades last about 5 days). With less money you must skip signals while your money is in use (first signal first):

Money (₹1L slots)Trades takenNet ₹Per year on that money2023202420252026
₹1 lakh (1 at a time)124 of 299−14,889−4.1%+2k−22k+4k+1k
₹2 lakh190−13,027−1.8%−9k−15k+10k0
₹3 lakh228+52,641+4.9%+12k+21k+20k0
₹5 lakh269+1,15,027+6.4%+31k+40k+48k−4k
₹8 lakh289+1,48,107+5.1%+49k+53k+56k−9k

Even at the best size (≈ ₹5 lakh) it earns about 6% a year on the money set aside, roughly what a fixed deposit pays and below what a Nifty index fund did in this period. With only ₹1–2 lakh it lost money, because which signals you can take depends on luck. "Simple" yearly return = total net ÷ money ÷ 3.6 years; idle money earning interest is not included.

Daily is clearly best. On 4-hour and 1-hour the trades are shorter (a "blue touches orange" sell comes within hours), many are sold the same day or next day, and charges eat the gains. 1-hour same-numbers barely trades (a 7% rise in 20 hours is rare).

High ROC levels — "only buy if ROC > 25" (30 Oct 2026)

Standard: ROC 20 > 729941.829+1,53,217+47k+53k+57k−4k97%
  • ROC > 25 makes a little money on daily (except ROC 200) but much less than the standard ROC 20 > 7. It only beats random buys about half the time, so the profit comes from picking strong stocks, not from good timing.
  • With a short ROC (20–30), > 25% is very rare (15–37 trades in almost 4 years: a 25% rise in a month).
  • Best daily ROC levels stay ROC 50 > 10–15 (+₹1.1–1.2L) and ROC 20 > 5–7 (+₹1.5–1.8L).
  • 4-hour is the one place a high level helps: ROC 150 > 25 = +₹1,11,918 (388 trades, beats random 97%), ROC 250 > 30 = +₹1,06,708, vs −₹6,729 for the standard numbers on 4-hour. But most of it came in 2024 (ROC 150 > 25: 2023 +5k · 2024 +95k · 2025 +12k · 2026 0), so it's less steady than daily ROC 20 > 7.
  • 1-hour loses at almost every length and level.

Stop-loss at the buy candle's low + ROC levels 3–30 % (30 Oct 2026)

Report: ../../../projects/trading-equation-backtests/reports/STRATEGY5_STOPLOSS_REPORT.md (script experiments/strategy5_stoploss.py). Every trade gets a stop at the low of the candle it was bought on. It sells at whichever comes first (price falls to that low, or blue touches orange); both trigger on a falling price, so the order inside a candle is never in doubt. ROC length 10–250 × level 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 15, 20, 25, 30 %, with and without the stop, all 5 timeframes.

Daily, ROC 20 (net ₹, all 50 stocks):

ROC 20 level> 3%> 4%> 5%> 6%> 7%> 8%> 9%> 10%
no stop+1.67L+1.69L+1.78L+1.67L+1.53L+76k+88k+68k
with stop+1.52L+1.54L+1.99L+1.85L+1.54L+81k+96k+70k
  • Standard ROC 20 > 7 with the stop: +₹1,54,307 vs +₹1,53,217 without, almost no change. The stop is about 2.2% below the buy price (median); it was hit on 67 of 299 trades.
  • It cuts the event-day crashes: the 3 Jun 2024 buys sold on 4 Jun at the stop: NTPC −₹4,959 (was −₹15,708), POWERGRID −₹3,847 (was −₹12,511), ULTRACEMCO −₹2,553 (was −₹4,728).
  • But it also cuts trades that dipped and then recovered, so overall the gains and losses cancel out. 2026 got slightly worse (−₹9.7k vs −₹3.9k).
  • ROC 20 > 5 with the stop = +₹1,98,764 (465 trades; 2023 +94k · 2024 +50k · 2025 +89k · 2026 −34k): highest total, but a bigger loss in 2026 than ROC 20 > 7.
  • Levels 8–10% are clearly worse than 5–7% (fewer trades, less profit). The sweet spot is ROC 20 > 5–7%.
  • On daily the stop hurts most other settings (total of all settings +₹48.5L → +₹29.0L; 75 → 66 positive). It only pays off when there are big sudden crashes.
  • On 4-hour the stop helps the long-ROC versions: ROC 250 > 30 = +₹1,41,710 with stop (vs +₹1,06,708); ROC 250 > 25 +₹1,34,157 (2023 +55k · 2024 +83k · 2025 +8k · 2026 −12k).
  • 15-min / 30-min / 1-hour still lose with or without the stop.

5. Other timeframes

  • 4-hour: only ROC 20 > 5 (any EMA) and ROC 10 > 2 hold up in both periods, for +₹5k to +₹24k. Too small after charges.
  • 15-min / 1-hour: nothing holds up. 30-min: 8 tiny winners (+₹5k range).

6. Lesson

For Strategy 5 the useful change is ROC 20 instead of ROC 100, with a 5–7% level, on daily candles: "the stock rose 5–7%+ in the last month and Stoch just turned up from below 50". It's the first version in all these tests that made money in each of 2023, 2024 and 2025 and nearly broke even in the falling 2026. Next: run it on Nifty 200 (stocks it hasn't seen) and paper-trade it.
